walkthroughs.body_html:
Component 3: Spoken Language Endorsement — a core area of GCSE English Language.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component 3: Spoken Language Endorsement brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component 3: Spoken Language Endorsement.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between descriptive and prescriptive approaches to language?
options: Descriptivists describe written language and prescriptivists describe spoken language.
Piaget was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.
Both terms mean the same — analysing language scientifically.
Descriptivists describe how language is actually used; prescriptivists rule on how language ought to be used — modern linguistics is descriptivist.

mcqs.q: How does Piaget's theory relate language to cognitive development?
options: Language develops as a consequence of cognitive development — children must first develop concepts (object permanence, conservation) before they can express them linguistically. Cognition leads language.
Piaget said language drives cognitive development.
Piaget was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.
Women and men have different vocal cords so speak differently.

mcqs.q: Are claims that women use more 'tentative' language well-supported?
options: Early studies (Lakoff) made broad claims, but later research (e.g. Holmes, Cameron) shows context matters more than gender, and many supposed differences disappear with proper data.
Women always use more hedges and tag questions than men.
Women and men have different vocal cords so speak differently.
Both terms mean the same — analysing language scientifically.
